summary.headline: Repco Home Finance posted record FY26 disbursements of Rs.4,148 Crores (+26% YoY) and cut GNPA to 2.55%, while AUM growth of 9.6% to Rs.15,880 Crores lagged disbursements.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly (Rs.1,186 Crores) and annual (Rs.4,148 Crores) disbursements, with Q4 PAT of Rs.129.11 Crores versus Rs.108.77 Crores in Q3. Gross NPA fell from 3.26% in December 2025 to 2.55% in March 2026, and Stage 2 assets declined to about 7% from about 9.5% a year earlier. Loan book growth remained well below disbursement growth because of run-off, prepayments and balance transfers out. Management guided to Rs.5,000 Crores disbursement and Rs.18,000 Crores AUM for FY27, and a 75% total FY26 dividend.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Tamil Nadu contributes about 60% of disbursements. Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Madhya Pradesh improved QoQ, and management expects non-TN states to contribute materially more from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Product and customer mix
segments.commentary: Home loans are 71% and non-housing loans 29% of the book, and salaried customers are 46% (Rs.7,410 Crores) against non-salaried 54% (Rs.8,470 Crores). Yields are 11.16% for HL, 13.44% for non-HL, 11.36% for salaried and 12.27% for non-salaried.

segments.name: New book (post-2022 loans)
segments.commentary: GNPA on the new book is about 1% and Stage 2 is about 3.9%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target of about Rs.5,000 Crores, with expected repayments and prepayments of about Rs.2,940 Crores and year-end AUM target of about Rs.18,000 Crores.
Management said Rs.25,000 Crores AUM is now targeted about two years out, implying FY29 versus the earlier FY28 aspiration.
Q1 FY27 disbursement plan is about Rs.1,000 Crores, with management aiming to keep quarterly disbursements above Rs.1,000 Crores.
Stage 2 assets expected to fall below 5% before end of FY27.
Spread target of about 3.2% to 3.25% for FY27, down from 3.34% previously reported.
NHB refinance of Rs.600 Crores sanctioned; expected to cut cost of funds by about 10 to 15 bps. Cost of funds expected to stay flat next quarter, and to rise if RBI raises repo.
CSR spend expected to return to about 2% to 3% of average profit, from 5% in FY26; exact figure to be given next call.
Dividend payout to be maintained at elevated levels per management, though the FY27 interim/final split and quantum were not specified.
capex_capacity: Network of 242 branches including SAT centres; nine offices opened in FY26.
Average disbursement per branch per month is Rs.1.5 Crores to Rs.2 Crores, with a model of one branch head and one branch sales manager per branch.
Approximately 180 to 185 branch sales managers; management is adding feet-on-street in non-TN branches and restructuring high-performance branches.
demand_pricing: Balance transfers out (BT Out) average about Rs.30 to Rs.35 Crores per month, mainly to public sector banks, while BT In averages about Rs.45 to Rs.50 Crores per month, mainly from HFCs for self-employed borrowers. Management says net BT In is positive.

FY26 principal run-off was about Rs.2,670 Crores, comprising about Rs.700 Crores scheduled repayment and about Rs.2,000 Crores of prepayments, pre-closures and BT Out (including Rs.400 Crores of BT Out, Rs.256 Crores partial prepayment and Rs.1,675 Crores full closure).
Management is following risk-based pricing and has cut rates case by case to retain customers. Benchmark rates were cut 10 bps on 1 July 2025 and 10 bps on 1 February 2026.
Competitive market: management says spread and growth are in tension and it will sacrifice some spread to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.25,000 Crores AUM by FY28 aspiration still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the original timeline. Management now targets about Rs.18,000 Crores by FY27 end and about Rs.25,000 Crores two years later, i.e. about one year behind. Inorganic buying is limited to Rs.25 to Rs.30 Crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is AUM growth well below disbursement growth, and is the new book also running down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed vintage run-off, self-employed customers making bullet and part prepayments, and BT Out. An analyst's data point suggested about Rs.3,000 Crores of run-off on the post-FY22 book; management acknowledged part prepayments on the new book but said there were no major pre-closures there.

qa_highlights.question: Can per-branch productivity support Rs.5,000 Crores disbursement with current sales staff?
qa_highlights.answer: Average disbursement per branch is Rs.1.5 to Rs.2 Crores per month, which management says is achievable with one branch head and one sales manager plus processing support. It also acknowledged that adding salespeople is an option but is constrained by cost-to-income targets.

qa_highlights.question: Will Stage 2 fall below 5% and how?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to get Stage 2 below 5% by the end of FY27. Rs.300 Crores was rolled back in FY26 through a dedicated collection vertical, and a separate team now targets B0 to B1 flows.

qa_highlights.question: Will the elevated dividend payout continue?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the higher payout is not a one-off and management wants to continue the trend. The FY27 interim/final split and quantum will be decided later.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the pricing and cost of funds trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds fell from 8.75% to 8.5% over the year, and the NHB refinance should cut it by 10 to 15 bps. Yield is about 11.9%, and spread is expected at about 3.2% to 3.25% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q-o-Q growth flat in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, and what is the fix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Karnataka e-Khata issue is fading, Andhra Pradesh had team realignment in Q4 with new leadership, and it expects growth from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. It expects a much larger non-TN contribution from Q1 or Q2 FY27.

risks_watch: Persistent prepayments and BT Out keep AUM growth (9.6% in FY26) well below disbursement growth. FY27 AUM target of Rs.18,000 Crores requires about Rs.2,060 Crores net addition.
Spread compression: yield fell to 11.9% from 12.07% while management targets a 3.2% to 3.25% spread, and cost of funds may rise if RBI raises repo.
Limited cost-of-funds relief: NHB refinance is worth about 10 to 15 bps, and bank borrowings (about 85% of funding) are MCLR-linked with no reduction expected.
Stage 2 target below 5% by FY27 end, versus about 7% now, depends on roll-back execution.
Sales productivity: a Rs.5,000 Crores target needs about Rs.1.5 to Rs.2 Crores per branch per month, and non-TN states remain weak.

Profit affected by one-offs of about Rs.46 Crores in FY26 (Labour Code Rs.15 Crores, silver jubilee Rs.5 Crores, CSR uplift Rs.15 Crores, daily-balance interest method Rs.11.53 Crores), with CSR expected to fall back to 2% to 3%.
Quarterly disbursement run-rate of about Rs.1,000 Crores to be sustained in Q1 FY27 (management guidance).
summary.management_tone: Confident on disbursements, asset quality and dividends, but cautious and sometimes evasive on AUM growth, pre-closures and spread, which management attributed to vintage run-off and competition. Several answers were vague on specifics (CSR, FY27 dividend split, sales headcount), and management promised follow-up on the next call.
